## SB_READ_ONLY is legacy now. What's the per-space replacement that stops all writes, including by admins, and what happens to member permissions?

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Install/Configuration.md] ---
### Legacy “single-space” mode options > Run mode

## Run mode
* `SB_READ_ONLY` *(legacy)*: If you want to run the SilverBullet client and server in read-only mode (you get the full SilverBullet client, but all edit functionality and commands are disabled), you can do this by setting this environment variable to a non-empty value. Upon the server start a full space index will happen, after which all write operations will be disabled. Prefer the per-space settings in the [[Dashboard]]: give the public read access to publish a space (see [[Publishing]]), or **Freeze this space** to stop all writes.

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Install/Configuration.md] ---
### Legacy “single-space” mode options > Web app manifest

## Web app manifest
Configure aspects of web app appearance as well as the authentication page:

* `SB_NAME`: Sets `name` and `short_name` members of web app manifest to whatever specified in `SB_NAME`
* `SB_DESCRIPTION`: Sets `description` member of web app manifest to whatever specified in `SB_DESCRIPTION`

--- [vault:corpus/docs/API/share.md] ---
### API > share.publishCollection(name)

## share.publishCollection(name)
Publishes a collection, the same as `Share: Collection`: first prepares the root’s transport with [[#share.ensureTransport(uri)]] (which may ask to connect or sign in), so the members’ URIs are those of the root’s [[#share:target:<uri>|target]] even when the transport was set up just now. Then resolves the collection and transforms every member with the collection as the share set (afresh, so baked content is current) (see `members` at [[#share.transform(text, ctx)]]), lists the root (letting the provider sign in, `{signIn = true}`), writes the members whose text differs from the remote (by the listed `hash`, or else by reading the member’s remote, one that can’t be read is written) and offers the listed files no member maps to for removal with [[API/editor#editor.pickMany|editor.pickMany]], every item unticked. Only ticked files are deleted. Writes and deletes go in one call to a [[#share:writeBatch:<root>]] service when the root has one, and otherwise through `net.writeURI` and `net.deleteURI` one by one.

Returns `{written, unchanged, removed, failed, cancelled?}`: the pages written, the pages left alone, the URIs deleted, and `{page?, uri, error}` for each write or delete that failed. `cancelled` is true when the batch service reported that the user cancelled it (for example dismissing GitHub’s commit message prompt): then nothing was written or deleted, and nothing counts as failed. ### Freeze a space

# Freeze a space
To make a published space read-only for everyone, including members and admins, check **Freeze this space** under **Space settings → Access**. Member permissions are kept for when you unfreeze it.

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Security Profiles.md] ---
### Software team

# Software team
A team, community, or any setup where a `write` member _might_ plant malicious content — deliberately or by having their own account compromised — for a more-privileged member (an admin, or a member of another space) to stumble into.

The recommended hardened profile:

* **Shell off** for spaces with untrusted writers. This removes the main capability an attacker could otherwise reach.
* **One hostname per space**, via a [[Dashboard#Bindings|custom-host binding]] rather than multiple path prefixes on one hostname. Use the primary URL for the `/.dashboard` admin surface through **Admin → Server**. Then configure a separate sub-domain per space. With this configured, the server rejects Dashboard APIs on space hosts and blocks browser requests to Dashboard APIs from other origins, including sibling subdomains.

**Why a hostname per space?** SilverBullet’s session cookie and browser origin are scoped to the hostname you’re on. A `write` member can make their space’s content run code as whoever opens it — but if each untrusted-writer space lives on its own hostname, that code runs in an origin that doesn’t hold another space’s session.

This profile benefits from wildcard DNS (or at least multiple sub-domains mapped) and a wildcard TLS certificate (or multiple custom-configured certificates).
